text:
alec: quick share — I ran a small cross-model quantization bench this morning covering Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B. Wanted to flag a couple oddities around fp8 vs int8 for kv-cache heavy generation. :bar_chart:

maria: nice, can you drop the numbers? batch sizes, seq len, and whether this used our continuous-batching path or the single-request fast-path?

alec: sure — tests were 1/4/8 batch, gen seq=1024, prompt=64. Used continuous-batching runtime with max_batch=16 and kv_cache hot-reuse enabled. Key takeaways: fp8 (our new kernel) gave 1.25x token/sec vs int8 for batch<=1, but for long-run reuse (many short requests reusing kv) int8 ended up ~1.1x faster due to fewer quant-dequant ops in KV hot path. p50/p95 latency varied: fp8 p50=45ms p95=120ms, int8 p50=52ms p95=110ms on A100.

devon: interesting — did the kernel selector pick fused fp8-attn kernels or fall back to mixed-precision matmul? any kernel fallbacks logged?

alec: kernel selector chose fp8-fused-attn for Mistral and Llama, but Qwen went to fallback mixed-precision for several layers (outlier ranges). I saw logs like: `kernel_selector: layer12 quant_range_outlier -> fallback mixed_gemm`

sophia: did you try per-layer calibration vs global scale? i've seen per-layer calibrations reduce fallback frequency on Qwen. also clipping on LN seemed to help in earlier runs.

alec: yes — ran 3 calib modes: global, per-tensor, per-channel (per-layer). Per-channel reduced fallbacks on Qwen from 9->2 layers and improved throughput ~8% on that model. However, per-channel calibration increased calibration time and slightly reduced sample quality on some prompts (BLEU/ROUGE style evals we run).

maria: can you share the exact calib steps/commands and the quant config? would like to replicate.

alec: pasted snippet below (ran on bench host with profile flags):
```bash
./rbench --model llama2-13b --quant fp8 --calib-mode per-channel --calib-samples 2048 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --kv-reuse true --kernel-policy auto
```
quant config used (abbreviated):
```
quant_format: fp8
calibration: per_channel
outlier_clip: 2.5
use_kv_cache_fastpath: true
fallback_policy: allow_mixed_precision
```

perfbot: profiler summary: avg tokens/sec (1batches): Llama2-13B fp8=620, int8=495; Mistral-7B fp8=1010, int8=980; Qwen-7B fp8=410 (with 2 layer fallbacks), int8=430. KV cache memory delta: fp8 -18% vs int8.

devon: thanks — do we have an A/B plan for shipping per-channel as default for Qwen-ish families? sounds like a win but the quality regressions worry me.

sophia: I'd suggest adding a lightweight eval sweep in rollout: run per-channel candidate and compare on customer's prompt set and our standard regen eval. If quality delta > threshold, fallback to global. Also add runtime telemetry for layer-fallback counts so we can safely roll out.

maria: agree. also we should update the batching heuristic: for heavy kv-reuse workloads prefer int8 path when reuse_ratio > 0.7, else prefer fp8 for single-run throughput. I'll open a PR with the heuristic rule.

alec: thanks — i'll upload the full csv of runs and raw profiler traces to the bench blob and link in the PR. preliminary findings attached in case it helps with heuristic tuning. :seedling:

perfbot: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1781234567/bench-results.tar.gz

maria: perfect. can we also annotate which layers dropped to fallback so model owners can check quant-sensitivity? that made a big difference when we patched Llama2 kernels before.

alec: will include per-layer map. planning a short run with 4096 calib samples to see if those last 2 fallbacks on Qwen disappear. will post results here.

sophia: thanks — super helpful. tagging @eng-platform to consider a runtime flag to prefer stability (avoid fallbacks) vs pure throughput.

devon: one more ask: can someone run the same across p4d to verify kernel perf differences? I suspect int8 vs fp8 tradeoffs shift on different hardware.

alec: agreed. next step: p4d run + extended calib sweep. will update thread.

maria: great, thanks alex — cc: @product for visibility on config defaults.
